advice: Propose an FP32 tile mapping experiment using the existing four ZA.S accumulators, with no change to the accumulation order or full output coverage. Process each 64-row band and 64-column panel as four 32×32 subtiles: ZA0 holds rows 0–31, columns 0–31; ZA1 holds rows 0–31, columns 32–63; ZA2 holds rows 32–63, columns 0–31; ZA3 holds rows 32–63, columns 32–63. Change only the order of accumulator extraction and stores: store the two column subtiles for rows 0–31 before extracting and storing the two for rows 32–63, then continue the existing panel traversal. This tests whether store order improves output locality while keeping all four FP32 tile selectors and the reduction unchanged. The mapping is a distinct tile-output schedule, not eight simultaneous accumulators. It is advice only; no performance effect is established.
risks: Store order may not improve locality because each 32×32 subtile is written with the existing row-major strides, and the changed order could worsen address or cache behavior. Verify that each output element is written exactly once, that all four ZA selectors map to the stated row and column ranges, and that full 512 output and general-size/tail behavior remain intact. Check n<=0, allocation-failure fallback, FP32 tolerance 0.002, unchanged ABI and thread count, and complete LIBXSMM BSD notices. If ranked for implementation, compare ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls under unchanged power settings; preserve each report’s best-of-three rule and apply the fixed promotion and held-out gates. Do not infer a cause from noisy scores.
